prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right contractor depends on your neighborhood, budget, the size/age of your home, whether your ductwork needs work, brand preference, and schedule. I can, however, tell you how to find the best company for your situation and what to look for when getting quotes.

Quick summary
- National/local firms that are commonly well-reviewed in Atlanta include Coolray and One Hour Heating & Air, but many excellent independent contractors serve the area too.
- Get written estimates from 3 reputable contractors, insist on a Manual J load calculation (not rule-of-thumb sizing), check licenses/insurance, and compare equipment, labor warranties, and SEER ratings.

How to choose the right company (step-by-step)
1. Gather 3 written bids
   - Ask for: equipment make/model and SEER rating, total price, itemized labor and materials, any work on ducts, permit costs, and timeline.
2. Require proper sizing and diagnostics
   - A Manual J load calculation is the industry standard to size the system correctly. Beware contractors who only estimate by square footage.
3. Verify credentials
   - Ask for proof of insurance and any required Georgia/local licensing.
   - Look for NATE-certified technicians and factory training for the brand they’re installing.
4. Compare warranties and service
   - Compare manufacturer warranties (parts/compressor) and what the contractor’s labor warranty covers and for how long.
   - Ask about available maintenance plans and response time for service calls.
5. Read reviews and check complaints
   - Check Google/Yelp, the Better Business Bureau, and local Facebook neighborhood groups for recent reviews.
6. Check for rebates/financing
   - Ask about utility rebates, manufacturer incentives, and financing options.

Questions to ask a contractor (sample)
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?
- What brand and model do you recommend and why?
- What’s included in the estimate? Any additional fees we should expect?
- Who will pull permits and handle inspections?
- What are the labor and parts warranties?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified or factory-trained?

Red flags
- High-pressure sales to “replace now” without inspection
- No written estimate or vague scope
- No proof of insurance or license
- Refusal to perform a Manual J or provide references

Ballpark costs (Atlanta area)
- Typical full replacement of a central AC for an average home: roughly $3,500–$10,000 depending on capacity, brand, SEER rating, and whether ductwork needs repair or replacement. Get exact bids to know for your home.

If you want, I can:
- Find 3 top-rated contractors near your zip code
- Help you compare estimates if you paste the written bids here
- Provide a short checklist you can print and take to appointments

Tell me your Atlanta zip code and any preferences (brand, budget, timeline), and I’ll find well-reviewed local options.
